question: What is the main goal of Essential Obstetric Care in clinical practice?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases in pregnancy
options.B: Reducing maternal and neonatal deaths from complications
options.C: Ensuring elective caesarean sections for all first-time mothers
options.D: Providing routine antenatal health education only

explanation: Essential Obstetric Care focuses specifically on treating life-threatening complications that happen during pregnancy, childbirth, and after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: Why is Essential Obstetric Care divided into basic and comprehensive levels?

options.A: To stop skilled birth attendants from performing deliveries
options.B: To separate antenatal care from postnatal care services
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To match service delivery capabilities with facility resource levels

explanation: Dividing care ensures smaller clinics handle what they can safely manage while quickly referring complex cases to bigger hospitals. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: How many specific medical functions must a health facility perform to be called a Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) center?
explanation: A health facility must be capable of executing all seven specific medical and obstetric interventions to be classified as a true BEmOC center. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: Which procedure is a required duty for Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC)?

options.A: Manual removal of a retained placenta
options.B: Conducting elective lower segment caesarean sections

explanation: Manual removal of the placenta and retained products of conception are core BEmOC responsibilities handled at primary health centers. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: What two extra services make Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmOC) different from BEmOC facilities?

options.D: Manual vacuum aspiration and antibiotic therapy

explanation: Comprehensive care adds blood banking services and major surgeries like caesarean sections to the standard BEmOC list. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: A woman in labor with a complete uterine rupture needs to be taken to a facility that offers which level of care?
explanation: Uterine rupture is a major surgical emergency that requires an immediate operation and blood transfusion, which are strictly CEmOC services. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: How much blood loss defines primary postpartum hemorrhage after a normal vaginal delivery?
explanation: Primary postpartum hemorrhage is clinically defined as losing more than 500 mL of blood within the first twenty-four hours after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: A pregnant woman comes in with severe frontal headaches, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What medication should the nurse-midwife prepare right away?
explanation: These signs point to severe pre-eclampsia, and magnesium sulphate is the drug used to prevent eclamptic fits. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: What does crossing the alert line on a partograph mean during active labor?

options.A: The baby has suddenly entered severe distress
options.B: Cervical dilation has reached ten centimeters complete
options.C: Labor is moving slower than normal and needs close monitoring
options.D: The second stage of labor has safely finished

explanation: The alert line acts as an early warning that cervical dilation is falling behind the expected rate of one centimetre per hour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: A nurse-midwife checking a partograph sees that cervical dilation has crossed the action line. What is the correct action to take?

options.A: Wait another four hours to see if labor picks up on its own
options.B: Stop all monitoring and give oral sedatives
options.C: Start immediate treatment or transfer to a comprehensive facility
options.D: Send the patient home with instructions to return tomorrow

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is delayed too long; prompt action like medical help or surgical delivery is required right away. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: Why is it important to soak used metal instruments in a chlorine solution before washing them?

options.A: To kill bloodborne germs and protect the people handling them
options.B: To lubricate the joints on speculums and needle holders
options.C: To remove rust and polish the metal surfaces
options.D: To sharpen the blades of surgical scissors

explanation: Decontamination is an initial safety step that kills infectious agents like HIV and Hepatitis viruses before cleaning and sterilizing. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: Which practice helps the most in preventing uterine infections in the labor ward?

options.A: Giving routine intravenous antibiotics to every patient
options.B: Stopping all family members from entering the delivery suite
options.C: Keeping unnecessary digital vaginal exams during labor to a minimum
options.D: Doing daily vaginal washes with antiseptic soaps

explanation: Limiting vaginal exams reduces the risk of pushing bacteria from the lower birth canal up into the sterile uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: In the 'three delays' model of maternal mortality, what does the second delay mean?

options.A: Delay in hospital staff starting surgery
options.B: Delay in reaching a health facility because of transport or distance
options.C: Delay in the family noticing a danger sign
options.D: Delay in the patient taking oral drugs at home

explanation: The second delay involves transport problems, bad roads, and long distances between communities and emergency clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: Before sending a patient with postpartum hemorrhage from a local clinic to a CEmOC hospital, what must the nurse-midwife do first?

options.A: Wait until the bleeding stops completely without medical help
options.B: Complete all financial billing paperwork before leaving
options.C: Stabilize vital signs and set up an intravenous (IV) line
options.D: Tell the patient to find her own transport

explanation: Stabilization, such as giving IV fluids and oxytocin, is necessary to keep the patient alive while traveling. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)
